TASK ID: exact-cover-to-sat

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Exact Cover to SAT. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Exact Cover and TARGET is SAT. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = ExactCover
Exact Cover.

Instance: {"universe_size": u, "sets": [[element, ...], ...]}
  * The universe is the elements 0..u-1.
  * Each set lists distinct elements of the universe, in any order. A set
    may be empty, and the same set may appear more than once.

Yes iff some of the sets contain every element of the universe exactly
once: the chosen sets are pairwise disjoint and their union is the whole
universe.

Edge cases: u = 0 is yes (choose no sets). Empty sets never matter. Two
copies of the same non-empty set can never both be chosen.

TARGET = Sat
SAT (CNF satisfiability).

Instance: {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[literal, ...], ...]}
  * Variables are 1..m. A literal is +v (v is true) or -v (v is false).
  * A clause is a list of any number of literals, including none.
    Literals may repeat, and a clause may contain both v and -v.
  * Literal order inside a clause and clause order do not matter. The
    same clause may appear more than once.
  * Variables need not all appear in a clause.

Yes iff some assignment of true/false to variables 1..m makes every
clause contain at least one true literal.

Edge cases: a formula with no clauses is satisfiable (yes). An empty
clause [] can never be satisfied, so any formula containing one is no.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-9iqludvq
All input files are in this directory; run every command from it and write your files here. problems.py provides SOURCE and TARGET with validate(instance) only. It has NO solvers and NO instance generators.

REQUIRED OUTPUT: create reduce.py in the workspace, defining
    reduce(instance) -> instance
It takes an instance of the source problem and returns an instance of the target problem, both in the formats documented in problems.py. The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

Before submitting, check your reduction. problems.py has no solvers, so first write your own brute-force solvers for both problems from the definitions above. Then write tests in test_reduce.py that compare your solvers' answers on many small source instances and their reductions, run them, and revise until the tests pass. Finally write verdict.json as {"verified": true or false, "tests_run": <int>, "tests_passed": <int>}, where verified is true only if all of your tests pass. Then submit.

"""Brute-force solvers for Exact Cover and SAT, written from the definitions."""

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import combinations


def solve_exact_cover(instance: dict) -> bool:
    u = instance["universe_size"]
    sets = instance["sets"]
    n = len(sets)
    target = set(range(u))
    for k in range(n + 1):
        for combo in combinations(range(n), k):
            covered = set()
            ok = True
            for idx in combo:
                s = set(sets[idx])
                if covered & s:  # not pairwise disjoint
                    ok = False
                    break
                covered |= s
            if ok and covered == target:
                return True
    return False


def solve_sat(instance: dict) -> bool:
    m = instance["num_vars"]
    clauses = instance["clauses"]
    for mask in range(1 << m):
        assignment = [(mask >> (v - 1)) & 1 == 1 for v in range(1, m + 1)]
        satisfied = True
        for clause in clauses:
            if not any(
                (lit > 0 and assignment[lit - 1]) or (lit < 0 and not assignment[-lit - 1])
                for lit in clause
            ):
                satisfied = False
                break
        if satisfied:
            return True
    return False

"""Polynomial-time reduction from Exact Cover to SAT.

Source: {"universe_size": u, "sets": [[element, ...], ...]}
Target: {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[literal, ...], ...]}

Idea: introduce one boolean variable x_i for each set i, meaning
"set i is chosen".

  * For every element e of the universe, add the clause
        (x_i1 or x_i2 or ... or x_ik)
    where i1..ik are exactly the sets that contain e.  This forces e to be
    covered by at least one chosen set.  If no set contains e the clause is
    empty, which is unsatisfiable -- exactly right.

  * For every pair of distinct sets i < j whose intersection is non-empty,
    add the clause
        (-x_i or -x_j)
    so that two chosen sets can never share an element.  This also handles
    duplicate non-empty sets (they overlap, so they cannot both be chosen).

Empty sets produce variables that are unconstrained (they cover nothing and
overlap nothing), which is harmless.  For u = 0 there are no element clauses
and no overlapping pairs, so the formula is empty and satisfiable, matching
the convention that u = 0 is yes.

The construction uses O(u + n^2) clauses of length at most n, so it runs in
polynomial time and never calls a solver.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any


def reduce(instance: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Reduce an Exact Cover instance to a SAT instance (CNF)."""
    universe_size = instance["universe_size"]
    sets = instance["sets"]
    num_sets = len(sets)

    # Precompute the element membership as python sets for fast intersection.
    set_elements = [set(s) for s in sets]

    clauses: list[list[int]] = []

    # 1. Coverage: every universe element must be in at least one chosen set.
    for element in range(universe_size):
        clause = [i + 1 for i in range(num_sets) if element in set_elements[i]]
        clauses.append(clause)

    # 2. Disjointness: overlapping sets cannot both be chosen.
    for i in range(num_sets):
        si = set_elements[i]
        for j in range(i + 1, num_sets):
            if not si.isdisjoint(set_elements[j]):
                clauses.append([-(i + 1), -(j + 1)])

    return {"num_vars": num_sets, "clauses": clauses}
